scope: Incubating component foundation. Product migration is separate.

components.title: Access list
components.summary: Who can reach a project: a member per row that opens them, multiple selection with the bulk bar and a locked owner.
behavior: A toolbar above the list says how many have access and offers Add member.
Members are link rows in a framed List with selection, an Avatar, the role as a Badge, how they got access, last use and a row menu.
Selecting rows raises a contained FloatingActionBar with Revoke access. The owner cannot be selected and its menu is disabled.
After a revoke, a status line in the list footer says how many lost access and Undo restores them.
accessibility: The List's select-all and row checkboxes are named for the member; the bulk bar is a named toolbar with a count status.
Machine and agent names are set in mono.
limitations: The host owns the members and persists revokes and restores.

shown.label: Owner locked, multiple selection with the bulk bar
Owner locked, multiple selection with the bulk bar
Owner locked, multiple selection with the bulk bar

use: Use AccessList for who can reach one project or resource, with roles in words and temporary access saying when it ends.
avoid: Color roles, or confirm every revoke with a dialog when Undo can restore it.
guidance.decision: Choose AccessList for a membership list with bulk changes. Use a Table when people need to sort, filter or export members.

rules.when: A member has a role or temporary access.
rules.do: Name the role in a Badge and say when temporary access ends, such as Read, 1 hour.
rules.avoid: Color-code roles or hide the expiry in a tooltip.
rules.reason: Words survive both themes and screen readers; color alone does not.

detect.how: Read each row's badge and description for the role and any expiry.

rules.when: A member cannot lose access, such as the owner.
rules.do: Make the row unselectable, disable its menu and say why in the description.
rules.avoid: Let the owner be selected and fail the bulk action.
rules.reason: A control that cannot succeed should not be offered.

detect.how: Select all and check the owner stays unselected.

states.guidance: Rows leave the list and the footer offers Undo.
A compact empty state says nobody else has access yet.

antiSlop.do: Say how each member got access in plain words.
antiSlop.avoid: Show internal policy identifiers as the description.
antiSlop.reason: People decide on access by who granted it and why.

checks.command: npm run ui:dev; open /design-system#access-list and exercise the documented interaction.

components.title: Activity log
components.summary: Who did what, one line per event, grouped by day with load more.
behavior: A plain small List with a section per day whose meta counts its events.
Each event shows the actor's Avatar, the actor and what happened, a Badge for machines and agents, and the time.
Load more adds skeleton rows under the existing rows and keeps the button busy; once everything is in, the footer says Showing 6 of 6 events.
accessibility: The list keeps existing rows while loading and announces Loading items.
limitations: For filtering, sorting or exporting events, use a Table such as the audit log.

use: Use ActivityLog for a short recent history beside an object, written actor first in the past tense.
avoid: Use it as the audit log, or write events in the passive voice.
guidance.decision: Choose ActivityLog for a readable recent history. Use Table for the searchable audit log.

rules.when: An event is written.
rules.do: Start with the actor and use the past tense, with keys and machine names in mono.
rules.avoid: Write passive events such as Secret was updated.
rules.reason: People scan the log for who did something.

detect.how: Read each title for actor first and past tense.

states.guidance: Skeleton rows appear under the rows already there.
The footer counts the events shown.

antiSlop.do: Keep times short and local; the section names the day.
antiSlop.avoid: Repeat the full date on every row.
antiSlop.reason: The day heading already carries it.

checks.command: npm run ui:dev; open /design-system#activity-log and exercise the documented interaction.

components.title: Animated collapse
components.summary: Reveal a region without leaving hidden descendants in the tab order.
behavior: Open state controls a grid-height transition; lazy mode mounts on first open and retains child state through later closes.
Initial open content appears without an entry animation; reduced motion opens and closes immediately.
accessibility: As soon as it starts closing, the content leaves the tab order and screen readers stop reading it.
Caller connects its trigger with aria-expanded and aria-controls.
limitations: Caller owns focus return if closing a region that contains focus.

omitted.reason: Cut to keep the page to the essentials; the animated-collapse fixture test renders it as "Eager connection details".
This family has no authored sm/md/lg size option. Its dimensions follow content or its container; examples preserve that API.

use: Provide a separate labeled disclosure trigger, choose lazy deliberately and move focus to that trigger before the host closes a focused region.
avoid: Treat AnimatedCollapse as a complete disclosure control or remount its children on every close to animate them.
guidance.decision: Choose AnimatedCollapse when an optional region needs a height transition. Use Collapsible for a labeled disclosure contract and Accordion for several sections.

rules.when: The region contains the currently focused control when it closes.
rules.do: Move focus to the disclosure trigger before closing and keep hidden descendants out of the tab order.
rules.avoid: Animate a region away while leaving keyboard focus in invisible content.
rules.reason: A visual transition does not resolve focus ownership.

detect.how: Close a region while a descendant has focus; focus reaches its disclosure trigger and Tab cannot enter hidden content, including with reduced motion.

states.guidance: Choose a focus return target before hiding focused content.
Keep the same open and closed meaning without relying on the animation.

antiSlop.do: Animate the actual disclosure height only when it helps continuity.
antiSlop.avoid: Add a delayed animated reveal to ordinary static instructions.
antiSlop.reason: Motion should explain a state change rather than make reading wait.

checks.command: npm run ui:dev; open /design-system#animated-collapse and exercise the documented interaction.

components.title: Announcements
components.summary: What's new, as cards that cycle in a 480px dialog with dots, Back and Next.
behavior: Each card has inert media, an eyebrow, a title, a line or two and an optional action link.
Cards slide in the direction of travel and the dialog eases to each card's height; reduced motion jumps.
Left and Right move and wrap around unless loop is false. Dots jump to a card. Next becomes Done on the last card and Done closes.
onSeen fires as each card shows, so the host can clear its unread count.
accessibility: The dialog is a carousel; each card is a slide named 2 of 4, and a polite live region reads the position and title on each change.
Focus starts on Next.
limitations: Swipe on touch is not implemented; use the dots or Back and Next.

omitted.reason: The dialog is always 480px wide and its height follows each card.

use: Use Announcements from a What's new row or button with a count of unseen cards, with three to five cards newest first.
avoid: Open it on its own over someone's work, or fill the media with illustrations or gradients.
guidance.decision: Choose Announcements for release notes people opt into. Use Banner for a standing condition and Toast for the result of an action.

rules.when: A card describes a new feature.
rules.do: Title it with what people can now do, such as Share a secret with a link that expires.
rules.avoid: Use the feature's internal name as the title.
rules.reason: A capability tells people why to care.

detect.how: Read each card title as an action someone can take today.

rules.when: A card has media.
rules.do: Show the real feature built from v4 components, made inert.
rules.avoid: Use screenshots, illustrations or gradients.
rules.reason: Real components stay accurate in both themes and at every corner setting.

detect.how: Inspect each media area for components rather than images.

states.guidance: Next reads Done and closes the dialog.
The host clears the unseen count from onSeen.

antiSlop.do: Keep the eyebrow to the area and the date.
antiSlop.avoid: Add exclamation marks or New badges to every card.
antiSlop.reason: The dialog already says these are new.

checks.command: npm run ui:dev; open /design-system#announcements and exercise the documented interaction.

components.title: Approval queue
components.summary: Requests waiting on you, each moving through new, pending, then resolved or failed in place.
behavior: A framed List titled Needs you with the waiting count as its action and a View history footer.
Actions sit in a second row under each request's text, so the age ends every title line in the same place.
New requests are unread. Pending shows the pressed action busy and disables its partner. Resolved rows stay with Undo. Failed rows take a bad icon tile, the error line and Retry.
accessibility: Each request title links to the request and marks the open one as current. Errors are announced as alerts.
limitations: The host owns request state and the approve, undo and retry calls.

shown.label: New, pending, resolved with undo, failed with retry
New, pending, resolved with undo, failed with retry
New, pending, resolved with undo, failed with retry
New, pending, resolved with undo, failed with retry

use: Use ApprovalQueue for requests that need the person's decision, with two actions at most per row.
avoid: Remove a resolved row while the page is open, or confirm an approval that Undo can take back.
guidance.decision: Choose ApprovalQueue for decisions waiting on someone. Use ActivityLog for what already happened.

rules.when: A request is resolved.
rules.do: Keep the row, put its title in the past tense and offer Undo; drop the header count instead.
rules.avoid: Remove the row as soon as it resolves.
rules.reason: Rows that vanish make people doubt what they just did.

detect.how: Approve a request and check the row stays with Undo and the count drops.

rules.when: A request fails.
rules.do: Say what broke and what to do in the error line and offer Retry.
rules.avoid: Show a generic failure with no next step.
rules.reason: The person can only recover if they know how.

detect.how: Read each failed row's error for a cause and a next step.

states.guidance: The pressed action is busy with a present participle; its partner is disabled.
A bad icon tile, the error line and Retry.

antiSlop.do: Name the object in mono and the person who asked in the description.
antiSlop.avoid: Title every row Approval request.
antiSlop.reason: People decide by what changes and who asked.

checks.command: npm run ui:dev; open /design-system#approval-queue and exercise the documented interaction.

components.title: Accordion
components.summary: Reveal related sections without leaving the current context.
behavior: Radix single mode uses a string value; multiple mode uses an array. onValueChange reports item values, and collapsible allows the open single item to close.
accessibility: Each trigger is a button inside a heading and controls its own panel. Arrow keys, Home and End move between triggers.
limitations: Disclosure does not persist a setting or validate its contents; the host owns those operations.

omitted.reason: Changes arrow-key direction only, nothing visible.
Changes arrow-key direction only, nothing visible.
This family has no authored sm/md/lg size option. Its dimensions follow content or its container; examples preserve that API.

use: Use stable item values and choose single or multiple mode from whether simultaneous reading is useful; allow long trigger text to wrap.
avoid: Encode required form choices in open sections or hide an unresolved validation error only inside a closed panel.
guidance.decision: Choose Accordion for several independently useful disclosure sections. Use Collapsible for one optional region and Tabs for peer views.

rules.when: A collapsed section contains invalid fields.
rules.do: Give each heading a distinct content name, reveal invalid content after submission and keep essential task instructions outside collapsed sections.
rules.avoid: Hide the only error explanation behind a closed Advanced panel.
rules.reason: People cannot repair a hidden field or complete a task from headings that conceal the instructions most of them need.

detect.how: Submit invalid content inside a closed item; the item opens, its named heading remains locatable and the invalid field can receive focus.

states.guidance: Choose single for one open section or multiple when users compare sections.
Reveal invalid content and move focus to its field after submission.

antiSlop.do: Write headings that identify the hidden content.
antiSlop.avoid: Use a stack of identical More details headings.
antiSlop.reason: Repeated headings make scanning and keyboard navigation ambiguous.

checks.command: npm run ui:dev; open /design-system#accordion and verify the documented interaction.

components.title: Alert
components.summary: Explain a persistent result or problem next to the affected content.
behavior: Alert supports tone and dismissal for inline feedback. Banner represents a standing condition above related content.
accessibility: Use readable text with the tone. Dismissal needs a named button and owner-controlled state when the notice can return.
limitations: Dismissal calls onDismiss; the owner removes or restores the notice and performs any recovery action.

omitted.reason: This family has no authored sm/md/lg size option. Its dimensions follow content or its container; examples preserve that API.

use: Use a concise inline condition with a supported tone and only the recovery or dismissal actions that the host can perform.
guidance.decision: Choose Alert for a condition that remains relevant beside the affected content. Use Toast for a recent transient result and AlertDialog before an irreversible action.

rules.when: A connection remains unavailable after a failed attempt.
rules.do: State which connection failed and offer a retry or recovery action beside the explanation.
rules.avoid: Show a generic Something went wrong banner at the top of an unrelated page.
rules.reason: The location and named object explain what the action will repair.

detect.how: Read the notice without its color. It still names the affected connection, current condition and available recovery, with no duplicate result announcement.

rules.when: An inline condition needs an explanation or recovery action.
rules.do: Choose info, ok, warn or bad from the actual condition, name the affected resource and give any recovery action a real handler.
rules.avoid: Use a warning tone for ordinary metadata, repeat the same success in Alert and Toast, or dismiss a blocking condition without another visible explanation.
rules.reason: Persistent notices consume attention and must explain a real condition where it can be acted on.

detect.how: Compare the notice with the current task state. Its tone, resource name, action and dismissal policy still make sense after failure and recovery.

states.guidance: Keep the condition visible until it clears or the owner dismisses it.
Remove the notice only when the owning state records dismissal.

antiSlop.do: Use one notice for one actionable condition.
antiSlop.avoid: Stack a success banner, success toast and green badge for one save.
antiSlop.reason: Duplicate feedback competes with the task and repeats announcements.

checks.command: npm run ui:dev; open /design-system#alert and verify the documented interaction.

components.title: Alert Dialog
components.summary: Confirm an irreversible consequence before performing it.
behavior: Controlled open/onOpenChange or defaultOpen owns visibility. Action and Cancel are Radix close controls; an async operation must explicitly control closing while it runs.
accessibility: Title and Description name the alert dialog. Focus starts on Cancel and returns to the trigger on close. The dialog stays inside the viewport, and Escape inside an open editor closes that editor first.
limitations: Action does not await a request or infer success; prevent its default close or control open while an async operation settles.

use: Control open state or prevent the Action default close, retain the resource and consequence text, and close only after the host confirms success.
avoid: Assume AlertDialogAction waits for a promise or close the confirmation before a failure can be shown.
guidance.decision: Choose AlertDialog when a specific irreversible consequence needs confirmation. Use Dialog for editable tasks and an inline action for easily reversible work.

rules.when: Deleting a named resource requires an asynchronous request.
rules.do: Name the resource and consequence, offer Cancel before submission, and close only after the request succeeds. Keep cancellation available while pending only if the host can actually cancel the operation.
rules.avoid: Use a generic Are you sure prompt whose action closes before the request settles.
rules.reason: The user needs the exact consequence and a retry path when the deletion fails.

detect.how: Confirm a failed asynchronous revocation; the dialog and error remain. Cancel works before submission, and pending cancellation is offered only if it actually stops the operation.

states.guidance: Control open state and prevent repeated destructive submission.
Keep the dialog open with the failed action and recovery text.

antiSlop.do: Label the action Delete connection or Revoke access.
antiSlop.avoid: Label both trigger and confirmation Continue.
antiSlop.reason: Vague labels hide which irreversible operation is being approved.

checks.command: npm run ui:dev; open /design-system#alert-dialog and verify the documented interaction.

components.title: Aspect Ratio
components.summary: Keep a media or preview region at a defined width-to-height ratio.
behavior: The ratio prop is width divided by height; Radix reserves that proportion while the outer container determines width.
accessibility: The wrapper adds no image alternative. Give the actual image alt text or name the embedded preview.
limitations: A fixed ratio can crop or letterbox media depending on the child's own object-fit behavior.

use: Set ratio to width divided by height, constrain its outer width and choose the image fit policy from whether cropping is acceptable.
avoid: Put instructions or form controls in a fixed-ratio box, or crop a meaningful diagram to fill an attractive shape.
guidance.decision: Choose AspectRatio for media with a known width-to-height shape. Use normal document flow for text, forms and resource details.

rules.when: A preview loads after the surrounding page renders.
rules.do: Constrain the outer width, set ratio to width divided by height, and give the media its own alternative text.
rules.avoid: Set a fixed-ratio shell around text that must grow with zoom or translation.
rules.reason: The wrapper reserves geometry; it cannot make overflowing text readable.

detect.how: Resize each media container before and after content loads; its width-to-height ratio remains correct and adjacent text can still wrap independently.

states.guidance: Reserve the same media area before and after the image arrives.
Let the outer width shrink while the selected ratio remains constant.

antiSlop.do: Choose a ratio from the actual media and show a readable caption or alternative.
antiSlop.avoid: Force the same fixed media shape around forms, text cards and every product illustration.
antiSlop.reason: A repeated shape can crop useful content or add empty space without serving the media.

checks.command: npm run ui:dev; open /design-system#aspect-ratio and verify the documented interaction.

components.title: Avatar
components.summary: Identify people and show grouped participants.
behavior: Avatar supports person, machine, agent and fallback identities, numeric size and optional status. Every kind shares one paint, a tint square with ink initials or icon and radius-control corners (square by default, 4px in soft mode); the initials or icon tell the kinds apart. Initials are 10, 12 and 14px at 24, 32 and 40px. The status dot is an 8px square outside the bottom corner with a 2px surface ring. AvatarGroup overlaps by 4px and exposes overflow, and Identity pairs a lead with text.
accessibility: Provide an identity name or accessible label. Organizations use text or a neutral icon, never an invented avatar.
limitations: Organization avatars are unsupported. Status is visual unless the owner supplies its meaning in the accessible label or nearby text.

omitted.reason: AvatarImage fills the same square, clipped to its corners. The fixtures hold no real photo, and a drawn stand-in would look like a defect.
A failed AvatarImage falls back to the initials, which every example already shows.
aria-hidden on an Avatar next to a visible name. It paints the same as person.

use: Choose the real person, machine, agent or fallback kind, keep a visible name beside Identity and make status meaning available in text.
avoid: Give an organization a person avatar, invent initials for anonymous identities or use a colored status dot as the only explanation.
guidance.decision: Choose Avatar for people, machine identities or agents with an explicit kind, and Identity when name and metadata belong together. Identify an organization with its name and a neutral building icon.

rules.when: Participants in the same member group have missing photos or different identity kinds.
rules.do: Keep names or meaningful fallbacks and make person, machine or agent kind explicit. Keep size and status differences tied to supplied meaning.
rules.avoid: Invent a profile photo or imply ownership, presence or rank through arbitrary size and colored dots.
rules.reason: Identity styling must preserve recognition without creating a false relationship or status.

detect.how: Remove all photos from a participant group. Names or meaningful fallbacks still identify members, and group size/status differences correspond to supplied data.

states.guidance: Keep readable fallback initials and the visible name.
Show the remaining participant count when the visible group is bounded.

antiSlop.do: Use consistent avatar sizes within one participant group.
antiSlop.avoid: Make one participant larger or add status dots without a real distinction.
antiSlop.reason: Unequal geometry implies a rank or presence state the data may not contain.

checks.command: npm run ui:dev; open /design-system#avatar and verify the documented interaction.

components.title: Badge
components.summary: Show a short status, version or environment beside its object.
behavior: tone is the one paint axis: outline, soft, solid and accent for metadata and emphasis; ok, warn, bad and info for status. variant is deprecated and maps to a tone (default solid, secondary soft, destructive bad, the rest outline). Badges are 20px (md) or 16px (sm) with radius-sm corners (square by default, 4px in soft mode) and one weight, and take an optional dot and mono content. Count is a separate 20px number chip: accent for attention, ink for weight and neutral for counts inside tabs and lists.
accessibility: Tone must accompany readable text; a dot alone does not explain status.
limitations: Badge and Count display caller-supplied values; they do not fetch or calculate status.

omitted.reason: Deprecated alias of tone="solid". Use tone.
Deprecated alias of tone="soft". Use tone.
Deprecated alias of tone="bad". Use tone.
Deprecated alias of tone="outline". Use tone.
Deprecated. It rendered as plain text, so it now maps to tone="outline".
Deprecated. It rendered as plain text, so it now maps to tone="outline".
asChild renders the Badge as the caller's anchor with the same tone paint. Badges label things; a destination belongs in a link.

use: Use Badge's sm or md treatment for compact status, Count for totals and quiet text for ordinary metadata.
guidance.decision: Choose Badge for compact object status and Count for a numeric total. Use Alert for an explanation and Button for an action.

rules.when: An environment, version and operational status appear beside the same resource.
rules.do: Use neutral text or a neutral Badge for category metadata. Pair status tones and dots with a real state label and its consequence.
rules.avoid: Color every environment or version as success, warning or failure without a corresponding state.
rules.reason: Category and operational state answer different questions; coloring both as status hides the exception that needs attention.

detect.how: Inspect labels with hue removed. Status remains understandable, while environment and version metadata do not falsely look like success or failure.

rules.when: A row includes status and a numeric total.
rules.do: Use Badge for a concise supplied status and Count for the number; keep an action in Button or a real slotted link.
rules.avoid: Render every metadata value as a colored badge, use a badge as an unlabeled button or invent Healthy from an absent status.
rules.reason: Status emphasis should distinguish meaningful conditions rather than decorate every fact.

detect.how: Read the row without color. Status text, totals and actions remain distinct, and each status can be traced to the supplied data.

states.guidance: Shorten the status term rather than shrinking its text.
Show a zero count only when zero is meaningful to the task.

antiSlop.do: Reserve status tones for actual status.
antiSlop.avoid: Add matching bright badges to every navigation label and heading.
antiSlop.reason: Repeated emphasis removes the distinction between ordinary metadata and an exception.

checks.command: npm run ui:dev; open /design-system#badge and verify the documented interaction.

components.title: Breadcrumb
components.summary: Show the current location and links to its ancestors.
behavior: Breadcrumb supports explicit parts or typed items, middle-path collapse and current ancestry. Product crumbs switch context and give way from outer labels inward at narrow widths.

A crumb with a menu is a switcher segment: its text and its standalone chevron button open the same Switcher, anchored to the segment's start. The segment draws no ground or padding; hover, press, open and focus states draw on the chevron.
lastIsCurrent={false} keeps every crumb an ancestor, for trails that sit above a page title.
accessibility: Use the breadcrumb landmark name and aria-current for the current location. Switching menus retain accessible labels when visible text collapses.
The chevron is the switcher's only tab stop and carries the popup attributes. Its name joins the menu label and the crumb's text, so the visible label stays hidden from assistive technology.
limitations: The owner supplies real destinations and switching callbacks; collapse does not implement routing.

omitted.reason: The switcher opens below its crumb by default; placement is a popover option.
Placement is a popover option and adds no breadcrumb behavior.
Placement is a popover option and adds no breadcrumb behavior.

use: Use real ancestor destinations and typed menu crumbs for actual context changes; retain the current location when middle items collapse.
avoid: Repeat the page title as a fake clickable ancestor or use a decorative separator character to combine unrelated metadata.
guidance.decision: Choose Breadcrumb for page ancestry. Use a context switcher for changing project or environment and Tabs for peer views.

rules.when: An ancestor link switches the local resource context.
rules.do: Use the actual resource name and preserve disclosure chevrons only for hierarchy or switching.
rules.avoid: Add a promotional call to action or a decorative arrow after every ancestor.
rules.reason: A path should predict the destination before activation.

detect.how: Activate every ancestor and confirm the displayed local context matches its label.

rules.when: A crumb switches the organization, project or environment.
rules.do: Pass menu on the crumb so the whole segment opens the Switcher and only the chevron highlights.
rules.avoid: Pad the segment or give it a hover ground, or wrap the label in a second focusable trigger.
rules.reason: Padding moves the root text off the content edge, and a second trigger doubles the keyboard path to the same popover.

detect.how: Hover and click the crumb text: only the chevron changes, and the popover opens from the segment's left edge.

rules.when: A deep resource page needs a route back to its parents.
rules.do: Link each ancestor and mark the final item as the current page; expose collapsed ancestors through the overflow control.
rules.avoid: Make every crumb a dropdown or repeat the entire path in the page title.
rules.reason: Ancestry should remain a short, predictable route through the hierarchy.

detect.how: Follow every ancestor and open collapsed items with the keyboard; each reaches the represented ancestor and the current item is not a false action.

states.guidance: Collapse intermediate ancestors while retaining access to them.
Render the current item without a misleading navigation action.

antiSlop.do: Use resource names and hierarchy labels.
antiSlop.avoid: Add slash-separated metadata such as region, role and expiry to the path.
antiSlop.reason: Those values describe the object but are not its ancestors.

checks.command: npm run ui:dev; open /design-system#breadcrumb and verify the documented interaction.

components.title: Button
components.summary: Trigger a named action with a clear emphasis and pending state.
behavior: Primary (and default, its alias) is the ink fill with an on-ink label at 600 for the one main action in a view or dialog; hover moves to text2. Accent keeps the bright lime face with owned inset illumination, for approval and grant moments only, never as a second primary. Ghost hover is ink at opacity-hover (6% light, 12% dark), so it shows on raised surfaces. Other variants retain their semantic roles. link is link-coloured text that underlines on hover. Native button and slot composition preserve interaction semantics.

The text sizes are 32px (default, with sm as its alias), 36px (md) and 40px (lg), with 10, 14 and 16px insets and the shared 14px label. icon matches default at 32px and icon-lg matches lg at 40px; iconOnly makes any text size square. xs, icon-xs (24px) and icon-sm (28px) are nested and chrome sizes. Nested control actions consume the host slot instead of inheriting a standalone action's geometry. Size names do not guarantee a touch target.
accessibility: Use a real button for an action and asChild with an anchor for navigation. Name icon-only buttons. Native disabled removes activation, while loading remains focusable and exposes busy/disabled semantics.
limitations: The owner runs the operation and updates loading. Button does not start requests, show result notifications or impose a destructive confirmation.
Button has no read-only prop. Use disabled for unavailable actions, or show read-only content without an action.

omitted.reason: Default is the alias of primary: the same ink fill.
A tint-filled peer of outline for dense toolbars. It adds no new decision to the comparison.
The quiet form of destructive for a row action next to other ghost actions. Same red text as destructive without the fill.
24px, below the 32/36/40 control scale. Reserved for actions nested inside another control, such as a chip or a field slot.
24px nested icon action, the icon partner of xs. Same reason as xs.
28px icon action for overlay chrome such as a dialog or sheet close. It sits inside a header, never beside text Buttons.
aria-invalid draws the red control border. A Button is rarely the invalid control; the field it opens carries the error.
selected sets aria-pressed and paints the shared selected recipe. Toggle shows that recipe; use Toggle for a persistent pressed choice.
Button has no read-only prop. Read-only content does not imply an available action; unavailable actions use disabled.
Button exposes loading and activation. Requests, draft persistence, results and retry are owned by its caller.
Button exposes loading and activation. Requests, draft persistence, results and retry are owned by its caller.

use: Choose emphasis with variant and geometry with size. default, primary and accent share one lime treatment; default and sm are size aliases. Give a pending action a leading icon when its label must stay visible while it works.
guidance.decision: Choose Button for an action. Use a native link for a destination, Toggle for a persistent pressed choice and Switch for an immediate setting.

rules.when: A form has one save action and several supporting actions.
rules.do: Use the shared lime Button for Save changes, use outline or ghost for Review draft and Discard, and keep the button's size and name while saving.
rules.avoid: Give every action the strongest lime emphasis, repaint the shared material in caller styles or replace Save changes with an unlabeled spinner.
rules.reason: Emphasis identifies the next action, while a stable name preserves task context during pending work.

detect.how: Toggle an explicitly supplied loading boolean. The action keeps its name and bounds, rejects repeat activation and retains visible keyboard focus in both themes.

rules.when: Primary and supporting actions appear beside one another.
rules.do: Use the supported size recipes for peer actions and keep the shared lime paint. Passing loading never changes padding, so pass it whenever the operation can become pending.
rules.avoid: Compensate for a borderless appearance with caller padding, add a new gradient or remove the action label while loading.
rules.reason: A shared size owns border-inclusive geometry; state and emphasis should not move the neighboring actions.

detect.how: Compare filled and outline peers at every supported text size, then enter pending and keyboard focus. Their outer heights and alignment remain stable without caller geometry patches.

states.guidance: Pass loading={pending}. The spinner overlays the button, so its width and padding stay the same whether loading is absent, false or true. With a leading icon the spinner replaces the icon and the label stays readable. Report success only after the actual operation completes.
Explain policy or prerequisites outside a disabled control because it cannot receive focus.

antiSlop.do: Write action labels that name the outcome.
antiSlop.avoid: Show default, primary, outline and ghost as the human-facing action labels.
antiSlop.reason: Variant names belong in comparison captions. Product action labels identify the outcome.

checks.command: npm run ui:dev; open /design-system#button and verify the documented interaction.

components.title: Button Group
components.summary: Join related actions without giving each its own container.
behavior: attached joins peer Buttons on a shared edge, so they read as one control: Older and Newer, or a split action. toolbar keeps each Button separate with a 4px gap and one tab stop; arrow keys and Home/End move among enabled actions, and ButtonGroupSeparator splits it into sets with one 1px line. spaced is a wrapping row with an 8px gap. ButtonGroupText is a non-interactive segment at the height of its neighbors. A separator between two outline Buttons is hidden, because their borders already draw the line.
accessibility: Name a toolbar for its action set; use ordinary groups when each button should keep its own tab stop.
limitations: Toolbar focus visits native button, link and role=button descendants; selection and action effects belong to the host.

omitted.reason: Layout only: separate Buttons in a wrapping row with an 8px gap, kept for a set that must wrap at narrow widths. It has no join and no keyboard model of its own.
The default. Both examples on this page are horizontal.
The same joins rotated for a narrow side panel: the shared edge moves from left/right to top/bottom and toolbar arrows become up/down.

use: Keep peer sizes aligned and use toolbar only for a named action set that benefits from roving focus; use spaced layout when attached actions cannot fit.
avoid: Mix unrelated action sizes, nest another focus system inside a toolbar or conceal essential actions beyond an unreachable edge.
guidance.decision: Choose ButtonGroup to join related actions. Use Tabs for peer panels, ToggleGroup for pressed choices and RadioGroup for one required value.

rules.when: Several compact tools act on the same resource.
rules.do: Group Inspect and Compare together, name the group, and use toolbar only when arrow-key focus is intended.
rules.avoid: Build an All, Reads, Writes view selector from ordinary grouped action buttons.
rules.reason: The shared edge signals related actions. It does not supply a selected-value model, and nonwrapping groups still need a usable narrow layout.

detect.how: At the narrowest supported width, reach every grouped action. Toolbar arrows move focus among enabled tools without changing a field or pretending to select a peer panel.

states.guidance: Keep a meaningful group label and allow arrow keys to move among enabled tools.
Use a spaced group or an outer wrapping layout when attached actions cannot fit.

antiSlop.do: Group tools by the object they affect.
antiSlop.avoid: Add a border around unrelated page actions simply to fill a toolbar.
antiSlop.reason: The shared edge implies a relationship that the actions do not have.

antiSlop.do: Name tools by the actual local operation and keep vertical focus movement aligned with the visible column.
antiSlop.avoid: Label every tool Action or simulate a completed network check without performing one.
antiSlop.reason: A group communicates related operations and a toolbar adds a specific keyboard axis.

checks.command: npm run ui:dev; open /design-system#button-group and verify the documented interaction.

components.title: Calendar
components.summary: Choose a date with keyboard-accessible month navigation.
behavior: Calendar forwards the installed DayPicker selection modes. In optional single mode selected is Date or undefined and onSelect may clear it; optional multiple mode uses Date[] or undefined, and range mode uses DateRange or undefined, including an unfinished range.
accessibility: Each day is announced by its full date, and arrow keys move between days. Label what the date is for and show a readable summary of the selected date.
limitations: Date values do not define a storage format. The host owns timezone and date-only serialization; do not derive a local calendar date by slicing a UTC ISO timestamp. Accept optional empty and incomplete range states.

shown.label: Date range with month and year controls

omitted.reason: mode="multiple" looks like single with several days marked and selected is a Date[]; the behavior notes cover it.
Without a mode the grid is the same and days are not selectable, so there is nothing to see.

shown.label: Date range with month and year controls

omitted.reason: Same as dropdown with only the month select; the year stays a plain label.
Same as dropdown with only the year select; the month stays a plain label.
This family has no authored sm/md/lg size option. Its dimensions follow content or its container; examples preserve that API.

use: Handle undefined and partial range values explicitly and serialize date-only choices using the host's intended calendar and timezone.
avoid: Slice a UTC timestamp to derive the displayed local day or treat the first range click as a complete booking.
guidance.decision: Choose Calendar for day-based selection with spatial date context. Use a text field for free-form input and a separate time control for an instant.

rules.when: The task asks for an expiry date rather than an exact UTC timestamp.
rules.do: Construct local calendar Dates and show a readable selected date; require both ends before submitting a range.
rules.avoid: Parse YYYY-MM-DD as an implicit UTC instant or treat a start-only range as complete.
rules.reason: Timezone conversion can shift a calendar day, and a partial range has no end date.

detect.how: Choose a local date and a start-only range across timezone settings; the calendar day remains the intended day and incomplete ranges cannot be submitted as complete.

states.guidance: Describe what date to choose without inventing a default expiry.
Announce the start-only state and request an end date before submission.

antiSlop.do: Display constraints such as weekdays and the selected result beside the calendar.
antiSlop.avoid: Decorate arbitrary dates with status dots that have no legend or task meaning.
antiSlop.reason: Unexplained marks create false availability or activity information.

components.title: Card
components.summary: Group one resource or task with its own header, content and actions.
behavior: Card offers framed and plain shells, a flush body and named title/description/media/action/footer slots. Framed (the default) is a tint frame with no border: its header row sits in the frame, with the title as an uppercase eyebrow and the action as a caption link, and the body and footer sit in an inner surface with a line border and shadow-raised. The inner surface is inset from the frame by space-3 on the sides and bottom, and on the top too when there is no header. Its radius is radius-panel minus that pad, so the corners stay concentric in soft mode and are square in square mode. Plain is a single surface with one line border and no frame. Title, description, body and footer share one text column; media hangs to its left and the action centres on the title line.
accessibility: Choose the heading level through the composed title; actions remain native controls with their own names.
limitations: Card adds no navigation role and does not choose a semantic heading level for title content.

omitted.reason: Both cards use the default size; their captions name the variant.
sm only narrows every inset from 16px to 12px; it adds no part or behavior.
flush only removes the body inset so a full-bleed table or list can bring its own; without that content it looks like framed.

use: Use plain or framed treatment for a distinct resource or task, with explicit content and action slots. Keep continuous sections open.
guidance.decision: Choose Card when one resource or task has its own heading, content and actions. Use plain sections for a continuous form and List for comparable rows.

rules.when: A resource card contains an Edit action and other independent controls.
rules.do: Keep navigation on the title link and actions on their own buttons.
rules.avoid: Make the whole card a button that contains nested links, switches or buttons.
rules.reason: Nested interactive targets create conflicting click and keyboard behavior.

detect.how: Tab through a card containing a title link and secondary controls; each target works separately and the card shell does not create a competing nested action.

rules.when: The same task can use plain or framed Card treatment.
rules.do: Keep the title's semantic rank and content meaning unchanged across variants, and use the named header, body, action and footer slots for aligned content.
rules.avoid: Make a framed title tiny uppercase metadata, add another padded wrapper inside every body or turn the entire card into a click target containing buttons.
rules.reason: Framing groups a task; it must not change hierarchy, double content insets or create nested interactions.

detect.how: Compare convenience props and explicit parts with identical content in plain and framed treatments. Title rank, content edges and action access stay consistent at narrow width.

states.guidance: Use a concise explanation inside the content area rather than an empty shell.
Let text and actions wrap without hiding the resource name.

antiSlop.do: Group one coherent task per card.
antiSlop.avoid: Wrap every label and metric in separate bordered cards.
antiSlop.reason: Excess shells hide the page hierarchy and waste space in dense work.

checks.command: npm run ui:dev; open /design-system#card and verify the documented interaction.

components.title: Carousel
components.summary: Browse a finite set of related panels with explicit previous and next controls.
behavior: Embla owns scroll position and reports its API through setApi. orientation chooses horizontal or vertical movement; previous/next disabled state follows the current scroll bounds.
accessibility: The wrapper and slides expose carousel/slide descriptions. Arrow handling follows orientation and leaves editable fields, composite controls and modified keys alone; navigation buttons remain explicit.
limitations: Autoplay is not enabled by the wrapper; any supplied plugin and its pause controls belong to the host.

examples.title: Multiple visible updates and current position

omitted.reason: Vertical movement swaps the scroll axis and the control positions; it adds no behavior the horizontal examples hide.
This family has no authored sm/md/lg size option. Its dimensions follow content or its container; examples preserve that API.
The host decides what an empty collection shows; the carousel renders its own slides only.
A single slide is the multiple-slide case with nothing to scroll to.

use: Show an honest empty result, derive position and previous/next availability from the carousel API, and keep all essential information outside hidden slides.
avoid: Invent a slide count, enable an action past a nonlooping bound or place required form steps in slides.
guidance.decision: Choose Carousel for optional browsing through a bounded set of previews. Use a list or grid when people must compare items or complete every step.

rules.when: Not all preview slides fit at once.
rules.do: Keep Previous and Next controls visible and identify the current slide or item.
rules.avoid: Put a required input or the only recovery action on an offscreen slide.
rules.reason: Hidden slides are easy to miss and make task completion depend on discovery.

detect.how: Use only keyboard and visible previous/next controls to inspect every slide; end controls report their boundaries and no required task depends on an unseen slide.

states.guidance: Disable unavailable previous or next actions at the ends.
Keep controls within the available layout and preserve access to slide content.

antiSlop.do: Use manual navigation for optional preview media.
antiSlop.avoid: Auto-advance a resource or setup carousel on a timer.
antiSlop.reason: Automatic movement changes reading and focus context without a request.

components.title: Chart
components.summary: Present numeric data with a shared legend and tooltip contract.
behavior: ChartContainer provides Recharts responsive sizing and a ChartConfig mapping series keys to labels, icons and color or light/dark values. Tooltip and legend content consume that context.
accessibility: Provide an equivalent text summary for decisions that cannot be read from the chart alone.
limitations: A chart tooltip does not replace an accessible data summary.

examples.title: Daily request counts with exact values

shown.label: Two series with the tooltip held open on Tuesday

omitted.reason: The tooltip appears only on hover, so a static page holds one open and shows dot. line swaps the swatch beside each tooltip row for a narrow bar.
Hover-only, like line. dashed draws the swatch as a dashed bar.
hideIndicator removes the swatch from the tooltip, which is only visible on hover.

shown.label: Two series with the tooltip held open on Tuesday

omitted.reason: This family has no authored sm/md/lg size option. Its dimensions follow content or its container; examples preserve that API.
Request lifecycle transitions belong to the host. The Human page compares loading, empty and error presentations directly.
Request lifecycle transitions belong to the host. The Human page compares loading, empty and error presentations directly.
Request lifecycle transitions belong to the host. The Human page compares loading, empty and error presentations directly.

use: Use ChartConfig to keep numeric series identity, units and accessible explanations stable across the data lifecycle.
guidance.decision: Choose Chart to compare numeric quantities or trends. Use Table for exact row inspection and include a text summary when values inform a decision.

rules.when: A bar chart compares request counts across days.
rules.do: Show the quantity and unit, a truthful scale, readable labels, and exact values outside pointer-only tooltips.
rules.avoid: Plot unlabeled bars with no scale or use color as the only series identifier.
rules.reason: Without units and exact values the visual cannot support a reliable comparison.

detect.how: Read the chart without hover or hue. The metric, unit, baseline, series identities and exact values required for the comparison are still available.

rules.when: Bars compare the same quantity across categories.
rules.do: Use a common zero baseline and the same unit; keep labels and exact values available when hover is unavailable.
rules.avoid: Start similar bar panels at unrelated nonzero baselines or change the unit without naming it.
rules.reason: Bar length encodes magnitude. Inconsistent scales can make a small difference look large.

detect.how: Compare the plotted lengths with their stated values and baseline; switching off hover or color does not remove the values needed for the decision.

rules.when: Numeric data changes between pending, empty, failed and loaded states.
rules.do: Keep series labels and semantic colors stable in ChartConfig, include units and an accessible summary, and show each data lifecycle truthfully.
rules.avoid: Plot placeholder zeros as actual observations, recolor series by array index or rely on hover alone for a consequential value.
rules.reason: A polished plot can still misrepresent missing data or reverse the meaning of a series.

detect.how: Compare the summary, legend, units and supplied observations after reload and failure. Missing observations are not reported as measured zero and exact values remain available outside hover.

states.guidance: Say that no observations match the period instead of drawing zero bars for unknown data.
Keep the chart region stable and distinguish pending data from a genuine zero count.

antiSlop.do: Use a consistent scale, restrained series palette and a visible unit.
antiSlop.avoid: Add decorative curves, perspective or color variation that changes no data distinction.
antiSlop.reason: The visual encoding should support a comparison rather than imply extra categories or precision.

components.title: Checkbox
components.summary: Stage an independent choice, including a mixed selection state.
behavior: Checkbox supports checked, unchecked and mixed values, labeled content and disabled policy states. The owner applies or stages its checked change.
accessibility: Name the control. Screen readers announce the mixed state.
limitations: onCheckedChange can report indeterminate; the convenience onChange maps only true to true. The owner computes aggregate mixed state.

omitted.reason: aria-invalid draws the red control border; Field shows the error rendering.
A stress case: a long label wraps beside the box, which stays top-aligned with the first line.

use: Compute checked and indeterminate from the actual eligible children, preserve policy-disabled selections and stage the boolean when a later Save applies it.
avoid: Treat indeterminate as true, count locked rows as selectable or use a Switch for a staged draft.
guidance.decision: Choose Checkbox for a staged independent choice or parent selection. Use RadioGroup for exactly one value and Switch for an immediately applied setting.

rules.when: A parent represents a subset of selected eligible rows.
rules.do: Show mixed when some children are selected and let the host compute checked state from the actual children.
rules.avoid: Treat mixed as checked or submit the checkbox's display string as permission truth.
rules.reason: The parent summarizes selection; it cannot establish authorization or prove every child is included.

detect.how: Select one child, then all eligible children, then clear them; the parent changes mixed/checked/unchecked and locked children retain their actual state.

states.guidance: Keep the parent label stable and expose indeterminate state.
Retain the reason an option cannot be selected beside the choice.

antiSlop.do: Describe the choice in a visible sentence or noun phrase.
antiSlop.avoid: Use a standalone tiny checkbox as an unexplained decorative selection marker.
antiSlop.reason: People need to know what checking it will include.

antiSlop.do: Keep checked, unchecked, mixed and policy-controlled choices inspectable with their visible labels.
antiSlop.avoid: Count a disabled policy selection as an editable choice or put the only reason inside an unreachable control.
antiSlop.reason: People need to distinguish their draft changes from selections the host requires.

checks.command: npm run ui:dev; open /design-system#checkbox and verify the documented interaction.

components.title: Collapsible
components.summary: Show optional details from a single trigger.
behavior: open/onOpenChange controls one disclosure; defaultOpen provides local initial state. Trigger toggles Content through the shared Radix root.
accessibility: Use a named trigger button. It announces whether the region is open and which region it controls, and the content stays ordinary content rather than a menu.
limitations: Collapsible coordinates one region; use Accordion when several sections need a shared single/multiple value contract.

omitted.reason: This family has no authored sm/md/lg size option. Its dimensions follow content or its container; examples preserve that API.

use: Keep Trigger and Content under the same Collapsible root, name the trigger for its content and choose controlled state when the host must coordinate closure.
avoid: Use the open boolean as the value of a saved setting or add decorative plus/minus glyphs with no working trigger.
guidance.decision: Choose Collapsible for one optional detail region. Use Accordion for several related sections and Switch for a saved boolean setting.

rules.when: A concise summary has supporting diagnostic detail.
rules.do: Keep the main task understandable while closed, use the disclosure for one optional detail and return focus before hiding a focused descendant.
rules.avoid: Hide prerequisites or the only recovery instructions merely to make the page shorter, or make opening details mutate a saved preference.
rules.reason: Disclosure reduces visible secondary content; it must not make essential work depend on discovering hidden instructions.

detect.how: Read the page with the region closed. The main task remains understandable, and opening or closing details does not mutate a saved setting or lose a focused draft.

states.guidance: Keep the trigger visible and the hidden content out of the tab order.
Reveal the region if it contains the field a submission requires the person to repair.

antiSlop.do: Hide genuinely secondary detail behind a named trigger.
antiSlop.avoid: Collapse every paragraph into More controls to make a page appear shorter.
antiSlop.reason: Repeated disclosure raises the cost of reading ordinary content.

checks.command: npm run ui:dev; open /design-system#collapsible and verify the documented interaction.

components.title: Command
components.summary: Find and execute an action using a searchable command list.
behavior: Groups rank label matches while keeping group order; pages drill into a nested command set. onQueryChange receives query and page ID; filter=false delegates filtering to the host.
Pending async commands reject duplicate activation, including the link shortcut; actual dialog close clears page, query and feedback before the next session.
accessibility: Arrow keys move through commands and skip disabled ones. Escape leaves a nested page before it closes the menu. Mod+Enter opens an enabled link that is not pending in a new tab.
limitations: Async action IDs stay disabled and busy until settlement. Actual dialog close resets query/page and notifies onQueryChange('', undefined); inline panels retain their query. Remote search, shortcut bindings shown on items and persistence remain host-owned.

omitted.reason: Inline embeds the palette in a page region. The examples show only the triggered dialog, and the inline mode shares its panel and rows.

use: Give commands stable unique ids, keep page groups meaningful and use filter=false only when the host actually supplies filtered results.
avoid: Use CommandMenu as a form value picker, show a shortcut that has no binding or treat closing as proof an action succeeded.
guidance.decision: Choose CommandMenu for searching destinations, objects and actions from one keyboard entry point. Use Combobox for selecting a field value.

rules.when: A command returns a promise that can reject.
rules.do: Keep the action named while pending, retain the command on failure and close only after it fulfills.
rules.avoid: Replace failure with a success notification or clear the query before the person can retry.
rules.reason: The visible command must report what the local operation actually did.

detect.how: Reject synchronization, retry the same command and confirm local completion follows fulfillment.

rules.when: The menu displays a keyboard shortcut for an action.
rules.do: Register that shortcut in the host and route selection to the same named action as the visible item.
rules.avoid: Display a shortcut cap that does nothing or treat typing as a committed action.
rules.reason: The menu should make real actions discoverable, not advertise nonexistent bindings.

detect.how: Search by a visible action label and invoke the displayed shortcut. Both activate the same real action; a typed query alone does not execute it.

states.guidance: Explain that no commands match the query and retain the query.
Keep asynchronous action feedback outside the closed menu when the action continues.

antiSlop.do: Group results by a meaningful type such as Pages and Resources.
antiSlop.avoid: Mix unlabeled destructive actions into a list of similarly named destinations.
antiSlop.reason: Search results must make the difference between navigation and mutation clear.

checks.command: npm run ui:dev; open /design-system#command-menu and verify the documented interaction.

components.title: Context Menu
components.summary: Expose secondary actions from a context menu.
behavior: Open menus retain Radix typeahead and directional keys. Shortcut text requires a matching host handler.
ContextMenu opens from its trigger's context action. Action items call onSelect and close; checkbox/radio items stay open unless closeOnSelect is true.
accessibility: The menu takes focus, arrow keys move between items and each item is announced as a menu item. Keep essential actions available through a visible control as well.
limitations: Provide another visible way to perform essential actions.
ContextMenu supports open/onOpenChange after interaction establishes the pointer anchor. There is no defaultOpen prop. Root content is positioned at the pointer.

omitted.reason: Both variants sit in the one menu: Connection details is the default row and Archive environment is destructive.
Both variants sit in the one menu: Connection details is the default row and Archive environment is destructive.
Inset reserves the icon column for a plain row beside rows that carry icons. The example menu has no icons.
A mixed state belongs to a tri-state parent choice the host owns; the example has none.

use: Provide a visible action path for essential operations and keep destructive consequences explicit in item labels and variant.
avoid: Make right-click the only path to edit or remove a resource, or pretend root content is anchored by a side prop.
guidance.decision: Choose ContextMenu for shortcuts on an already discoverable object. Use DropdownMenu when the action entry point must be visible.

rules.when: An essential action appears in a right-click menu.
rules.do: Provide the same action through a visible button or menu, and make the context trigger keyboard reachable.
rules.avoid: Make right-click the only way to inspect, copy or restore an object.
rules.reason: Touch users and people who do not discover context menus still need the action.

detect.how: Complete the essential object action without right-clicking; the visible alternative and Shift+F10 context route both reach the intended action.

states.guidance: Explain why a locked action is unavailable in surrounding object detail.
Announce copied only after the clipboard write fulfills; show a failure if it rejects.

antiSlop.do: Name menu actions for the object under the pointer.
antiSlop.avoid: Fill the menu with disabled coming-soon entries.
antiSlop.reason: Unavailable placeholders hide the actions a person can use now.

checks.command: npm run ui:dev; open /design-system#context-menu and verify the documented interaction.

components.title: Dialog
components.summary: Edit or inspect a task in a modal with a title and description.
behavior: open/onOpenChange or defaultOpen controls the Radix dialog. Trigger and Close compose native controls; scoped Content portals into V4Scope and scrolls within the viewport.
accessibility: Title and Description name the dialog. Focus stays inside it and returns to the trigger. Escape inside an open editor closes that editor before the dialog.
limitations: Dialog does not submit forms, await requests or choose success/error copy; the task owner controls those states and closure.

use: Keep a named DialogTitle and useful description, let the task owner manage pending/error/open state and keep the failed draft inside the dialog.
avoid: Wrap an async submit in an unconditional close control or remove the only close path without a deliberate pending policy.
guidance.decision: Choose Dialog for a focused editable task. Use AlertDialog for irreversible confirmation and Sheet for supporting details kept beside the page.

rules.when: A focused task includes a long history or a rejected form submission.
rules.do: Keep long content inside the viewport and retain the entered draft beside its error.
rules.avoid: Use a short happy-path fixture as the only sizing check or celebrate an unfulfilled save.
rules.reason: A modal must preserve the repair path even when content and text enlarge.

detect.how: Open the long history at 320px and 200% text, then reject a changed name and retry without losing the draft.

rules.when: Saving a modal form can fail.
rules.do: Keep the dialog open while saving, retain the draft on rejection, and place the error beside the form.
rules.avoid: Close on submit and show success before awaiting the result.
rules.reason: Closing loses the repair context and can falsely claim persistence.

detect.how: Submit a failing save, correct it and retry. The draft survives failure, the dialog closes only on confirmed completion and focus returns to a logical target.

states.guidance: Give the dialog a specific title and an initial focus target.
Make the host's dismissal policy explicit before a draft is discarded.

antiSlop.do: Keep one focused task and its necessary context in the dialog.
antiSlop.avoid: Recreate a full settings page with nested navigation inside a small modal.
antiSlop.reason: A crowded modal makes orientation and recovery harder than a page would.

checks.command: npm run ui:dev; open /design-system#dialog and verify the documented interaction.

components.title: Drawer
components.summary: Present a modal panel that opens from a screen edge.
behavior: DrawerBody owns the shared body inset and bounded scrolling between Header and Footer. It forwards a div ref and native props; Content continues to accept arbitrary children. Use one intentional scroll owner.
Drawer forwards Vaul's controlled open/onOpenChange, direction and drag behavior; its Content and Overlay portal into the current V4Scope.
accessibility: Provide DrawerTitle and DrawerDescription. Focus stays inside the open drawer and returns to the trigger. Escape inside an open editor closes the editor before the drawer.
limitations: Drag thresholds and dismissal are Vaul behavior; the host must choose whether a pending task may be dismissed.

use: Choose direction from the task layout, give the drawer a title and decide whether dismissal is allowed while the host operation is pending.
avoid: Use a drag gesture as the only close path or allow a pending task to disappear without a defined draft policy.
guidance.decision: Choose Drawer for a dismissible edge panel where drag interaction is useful. Use Sheet for a side task without a drag model and Dialog for a centered focused task.

rules.when: A drawer can be dismissed by a gesture.
rules.do: Provide a visible close control and protect a dirty draft through host-controlled open state.
rules.avoid: Make swipe the only exit or connect a drag gesture to irreversible work.
rules.reason: Gestures need an equivalent discoverable control and must not silently commit work.

detect.how: Open and close the panel without a swipe, then test a dirty draft. The visible exit works and host dismissal cannot silently lose unsaved input.

states.guidance: Keep title and dismissal visible within the panel.
Prevent a host operation from being mistaken for a completed action when the drawer closes.

antiSlop.do: Use the panel for one supporting task.
antiSlop.avoid: Layer several drawers to imitate page navigation.
antiSlop.reason: Stacked edge panels obscure origin, focus and the remaining task.

checks.command: npm run ui:dev; open /design-system#drawer and verify the documented interaction.

components.title: Dropdown Menu
components.summary: Choose an action or setting from a trigger menu.
behavior: Open menus retain Radix typeahead and directional keys. Shortcut text requires a matching host handler.
Radix Root owns open/onOpenChange. Action items close after onSelect; checkbox/radio changes stay open by default and can opt into closeOnSelect.
accessibility: A named trigger opens the menu. Typing a letter jumps to a matching item, arrow keys skip disabled items and focus returns to the trigger on close. Use checkbox or radio items for persistent selection.
limitations: Menu checked state and action effects are caller-owned; menu dismissal does not mean an operation succeeded.

omitted.reason: Inset reserves the icon column for a plain row beside rows that carry icons. The example menu has no icons.

use: Use Item, CheckboxItem and RadioItem for their actual action or value contract, and prevent default dismissal only when continued interaction is needed.
avoid: Style ordinary items to look checked, add buttons inside menu items or announce success merely because the menu closed.
guidance.decision: Choose DropdownMenu for a short set of actions or checked preferences behind a visible trigger. Use Popover for editable controls and Select for a form value.

rules.when: A menu includes a dangerous operation among ordinary actions.
rules.do: Separate the destructive item, name its consequence, and let the host confirm when necessary.
rules.avoid: Put a multi-field form or an unguarded irreversible action in a generic More menu.
rules.reason: Menu selection closes quickly and is unsuitable for a draft that needs validation.

detect.how: Use the menu with keyboard only. Action items do what their labels name, checked items reflect owner state and editable tasks use a suitable form surface.

states.guidance: Control checkbox and radio items from actual preference state.
Keep continuing operation feedback outside the menu after it closes.

antiSlop.do: Keep the trigger label tied to the object or action set.
antiSlop.avoid: Use several adjacent unlabeled ellipsis buttons for different action sets.
antiSlop.reason: Identical hidden menus make the correct action hard to locate.

checks.command: npm run ui:dev; open /design-system#dropdown-menu and verify the documented interaction.

components.title: Empty
components.summary: Explain why a collection has no items and how to create one.
behavior: EmptyState composes title, description, icon and action slots in default or compact form; the retained Empty parts support a custom arrangement.
accessibility: Use a meaningful heading and a named native action. The empty container does not automatically announce asynchronous changes.
limitations: The caller distinguishes an empty result from loading, failure and missing permission; EmptyState does not fetch data.

examples.title: No connections and a creation entry point

omitted.reason: This family has no authored sm/md/lg size option. Its dimensions follow content or its container; examples preserve that API.

use: Distinguish first use, no matches, missing permission and request failure; choose an action that resolves that specific condition.
avoid: Show Create your first item after a failed request or repeat a large illustration and paragraph in every small empty region.
guidance.decision: Choose EmptyState to explain why a collection has no rows. Use an error notice for a failed request and a loading state while the result is unknown.

rules.when: A filtered collection contains no matching rows.
rules.do: Say that no results match and offer Clear filters when it can help.
rules.avoid: Show a first-use Create resource prompt for a failed request or a filtered result.
rules.reason: First use, a filtered result and a failed request require different next actions. A polished empty shell cannot establish which cause occurred.

detect.how: Compare initial-empty, filtered-empty, loading and failure content. Each states the established cause and offers only an applicable next action.

states.guidance: Explain what the collection holds and offer the permitted creation action.
Keep filter context visible and offer a reset rather than implying all data is absent.

antiSlop.do: Use the smallest useful explanation and one relevant next action.
antiSlop.avoid: Add a large celebratory illustration and several unrelated calls to action.
antiSlop.reason: The empty region should help the person resume work rather than compete with the page.

checks.command: npm run ui:dev; open /design-system#empty-state and verify the documented interaction.

components.title: Field
components.summary: Connect a control to its label, description and validation error.
behavior: Use label/description/error shorthand around one control for automatic ID, label, described-by and invalid-state association. Compound FieldLabel/FieldDescription/FieldError parts remain available for custom layouts. An error renders one way everywhere: a red alert icon and the message, several messages stacked under one icon. The label stays ink; the control's red border and the message carry the error. The label sits 6px above the control (the field-label space token).
accessibility: The short form connects the label, help and error to a single control. In a compound layout, match htmlFor to the control's id and point aria-describedby at the help and error. Grouped controls take a group with a legend.
limitations: Automatic association is limited to controls consuming Field context. Custom controls and compound parts need explicit IDs and ARIA wiring; validation is host-owned.

omitted.reason: Vertical below the field group's md container width and horizontal above it. At this page width it is identical to horizontal.
A legend set in the field-label type instead of the section title, for a short group inside a form. Same element and association as legend.
FieldLegend variant="label"; see the FieldLegend.variant axis.

use: Use vertical, horizontal or responsive Field composition to keep a value's visible name, help and correction together.
guidance.decision: Choose Field to connect a control with its label, help and error. Use FieldSet and FieldLegend for a group rather than assigning one label to several controls.

rules.when: A control fails validation after submission.
rules.do: Keep the entered value, associate the field-specific error with the focusable control and explain the repair without repeating the label.
rules.avoid: Put an error beside an unlabeled wrapper or show unrelated help and error as competing instructions.
rules.reason: The person needs one clear repair instruction attached to the value they can change, not repeated helper copy competing with the error.

detect.how: Activate each visible label and inspect the focused control's accessible description. Its own help/error is associated, and entered values survive invalid submission.

rules.when: A form control has a label, help and validation error.
rules.do: Use Field for supported automatic association, or connect explicit ids and ARIA descriptions for custom and compound controls; keep the label visible.
rules.avoid: Assume every child consumes Field context, use placeholder text as the label or show an invalid color with no associated explanation.
rules.reason: Visual proximity does not create an accessible label or tell the person how to correct the value.

detect.how: Focus each control with an error and inspect its name and description associations. The visible error is reachable, and custom controls retain explicit wiring.

states.guidance: Mark optionality in the label area without replacing the control name.
Retain the entered value and use an actionable field-specific error.

antiSlop.do: Write help only when it changes how a person fills the field.
antiSlop.avoid: Repeat the label as placeholder, description and tooltip.
antiSlop.reason: Repeated copy creates noise without adding a constraint or example.

antiSlop.do: Associate each error with the editable control and preserve exact values while repairing it.
antiSlop.avoid: Replace task-specific errors with a generic invalid badge or normalize a machine identifier in help text.
antiSlop.reason: The person must be able to locate the value and understand what can repair it.

components.title: Hover Card
components.summary: Show supplementary information on hover or keyboard focus.
behavior: Radix HoverCard owns open/onOpenChange and hover delays; Content is scoped to V4Scope and accepts alignment and side offset.
accessibility: HoverCard is supplementary preview content, not a keyboard task surface. Keep the trigger's destination and essential information available without opening it.
limitations: Keep essential instructions and actions in persistent content rather than only in the hover card.

use: Keep the link destination and necessary information in persistent content, then use HoverCard for optional supporting details.
avoid: Put the only permission explanation or an essential edit action inside hover-only content.
guidance.decision: Choose HoverCard for optional supporting information about a visible link. Use Popover for an intentional interactive panel and Tooltip for a short control explanation.

rules.when: A linked identity has an email and role preview.
rules.do: Keep the visible link sufficient to identify the destination and show optional details in the preview.
rules.avoid: Hide required instructions, permission explanations or task controls only in the hover preview, or make its only destination a dead link.
rules.reason: Hover previews are supplemental and cannot be the only route to complete the task.

detect.how: Use the linked object without opening its preview. Required identity, destination and task instructions remain available, and keyboard focus can reveal supplemental information.

states.guidance: Ensure the trigger remains a meaningful keyboard-accessible link.
Omit unknown metadata rather than presenting invented identity details.

antiSlop.do: Keep the preview concise and tied to the linked object.
antiSlop.avoid: Turn every noun on the page into a rich hover card.
antiSlop.reason: Excess previews distract from reading and do not replace page hierarchy.

components.title: Input
components.summary: Enter a single-line value with native input behavior.
behavior: Input forwards its native ref and supports sm/md/lg at 32/36/40px, defaulting to sm32, with icon, mono, a read-only lock and trailing content while retaining native editing. A native numeric size is a width hint and retains the default 32px density.
accessibility: Associate a label using Field or explicit htmlFor/id; use readOnly when the value must remain selectable.
limitations: Input keeps native input types and callbacks; formatting, validation and persistence belong to the host. Use Textarea for multiple lines.

use: Choose sm, md or lg for one-line editing. Use supported icon and trailing slots, and mono only for a technical value.
guidance.decision: Choose Input for a single-line value with native editing. Use Textarea for multiple lines and SensitiveEditor when stored secret retrieval must be deferred.

rules.when: A value is readable and copyable but cannot be edited.
rules.do: Use readOnly and retain a visible label and selectable value.
rules.avoid: Disable the field solely to prevent editing when the task still requires copying.
rules.reason: Disabled controls cannot receive focus and can block ordinary selection.

detect.how: Edit, copy a read-only value and submit an invalid draft. The field keeps its persistent name and exact value; readonly does not accidentally become disabled.

rules.when: A one-line value includes an icon, suffix or trailing control.
rules.do: Use Input's supported size, mono, icon and trailing options, preserve a visible label and keep read-only distinct from disabled.
rules.avoid: Pad the input locally to fit a suffix, register a shortcut only by setting kbd or format an exact identifier on every keystroke.
rules.reason: The owned slots prevent collisions; displayed affordances do not implement shortcuts or value transformations.

detect.how: Type a long value beside a long suffix, then test read-only, invalid and disabled states. Text and trailing controls stay separate and the original value is preserved.

states.guidance: Retain the draft and associate the error with the input.
Use an example placeholder only after supplying a persistent visible label.

antiSlop.do: Choose a width that reflects the expected value.
antiSlop.avoid: Stretch a two-digit field across the page or squeeze a resource path into a tiny box.
antiSlop.reason: Field measure communicates the expected input and affects review accuracy.

antiSlop.do: Compare density with the same value, and include empty, long exact-value and read-only cases.
antiSlop.avoid: Treat the native numeric size hint as another density or only test friendly short names.
antiSlop.reason: Geometry and editing behavior are different contracts, and long identifiers expose hidden padding mistakes.
