components.title: Input Group
components.summary: Compose a text input with leading and trailing controls.
behavior: The default host is sm32; explicit md36 and lg40 retain 24/28/32px nested action slots. Nested buttons fit the host slot even when a larger standalone size is requested.
InputGroup supports sm/md/lg, joined addons and actions, plus Field association. Addons do not become a second input.
accessibility: Keep one named editable control in each input group. Action buttons need separate names.
limitations: Addon click-to-focus ignores nested interactive controls; it does not register keyboard shortcuts or write to the clipboard.

use: Build compound fields from the shared control, addon and action parts instead of assembling another independently styled field.
guidance.decision: Choose InputGroup when one value has a prefix, suffix or adjacent tool. Use FieldGroup for several independent values.

rules.when: A URL field has a scheme prefix and a clear action.
rules.do: Keep one editable input, make the prefix part of the visible context, and name the clear button.
rules.avoid: Put a second editable value inside an addon or make the prefix look editable when it is not.
rules.reason: The group should still describe one value with one label and error.

detect.how: Name and operate the group with keyboard only. There is one intended editable value, and prefix/suffix or clear actions do not become a second ambiguous field or submit the form.

rules.when: A field includes prefixes, suffixes or an embedded action.
rules.do: Use InputGroupAddon and InputGroupButton with the host size, keep labels outside the editable value and let nested controls retain their own activation.
rules.avoid: Place a full standalone Button inside the field with caller height patches, or let clicking Copy focus and alter the input instead.
rules.reason: The host and its action need compatible geometry and separate interaction ownership.

detect.how: Compare sm, md and lg groups with text and icon actions. Nested activation does its named work, does not trigger addon focus behavior and does not enlarge the host unexpectedly.

states.guidance: Keep units or scheme visible when they are necessary to interpret the empty value.
Clear the intended input without submitting the enclosing form.

antiSlop.do: Use addons for units and tools that act on this value.
antiSlop.avoid: Add decorative icons and badges to both sides of every field.
antiSlop.reason: Extra chrome reduces space for the value without improving the decision.

antiSlop.do: Keep addons around one editable value and make every embedded action update that value.
antiSlop.avoid: Show a decorative Clear action or infer an inner action height from the outer group size.
antiSlop.reason: Addons share context without changing the input identity or the action recipe.

checks.command: npm run ui:dev; open /design-system#input-group and verify the documented interaction.

components.title: Input OTP
components.summary: Enter a fixed-length verification code in connected slots.
behavior: One underlying input owns the whole string; onChange receives that string, including partial and empty values. maxLength defines completion; onComplete signals length completion, not successful verification.
accessibility: Put id, label and error associations on InputOTP's real input. Slots display characters and focus position; they are not separate inputs. Paste and one-time-code autofill use that whole input.
limitations: inputMode only suggests a keyboard; set pattern for numeric or alphanumeric codes explicitly. The library defaults autocomplete to one-time-code and supports pasteTransformer; the host owns verification, retries and rate limits.

use: Keep a code as one string. Configure its accepted characters and length before connecting completion to host verification.
guidance.decision: Choose InputOTP for a short verification code with a known pattern and length. Use Input for arbitrary tokens or long recovery strings.

rules.when: The last slot becomes filled.
rules.do: Keep the code as one string and let the host verify it before announcing authentication success.
rules.avoid: Store each slot separately or equate reaching maxLength with a verified code.
rules.reason: A complete code can still be wrong, expired or rejected by the server.

detect.how: Paste a complete code, delete to a partial code and reject verification; one string stays editable and filling the final slot does not announce authentication success.

rules.when: A verification form accepts a fixed-length code.
rules.do: Set the accepted pattern and length deliberately, allow paste through the supported transformer and let the host verify and rate-limit submissions.
rules.avoid: Assume inputMode enforces digits or show Verified when onComplete only means every slot is filled.
rules.reason: Completing an entry is different from a server accepting the code.

detect.how: Paste valid and invalid characters, fill the final slot and reject verification. The entry contract holds and completion never reports authentication success by itself.

states.guidance: Allow empty and intermediate values so deletion and paste remain usable.
Keep a clear verification error and explain whether the person should retry or request a new code.

antiSlop.do: Use separators only where the issued code has meaningful groups.
antiSlop.avoid: Style each slot like a separate form with its own label and error.
antiSlop.reason: The code is one value and should behave like one editing target.

antiSlop.do: Keep the slot count consistent with maxLength and show partial, complete and rejected local values.
antiSlop.avoid: Treat completion as successful authentication or present different slot groupings as named sizes.
antiSlop.reason: Completion reports a whole local value; verification and persistence belong to the host.

checks.command: npm run ui:dev; open /design-system#input-otp and verify the documented interaction.

components.title: Item
components.summary: Arrange one object with its title, description, media and actions.
behavior: Item composes rows with title, media, metadata, actions, error/unread states and actions below the text. ItemGroup keeps the requested semantic wrapper; Tile is a native selected button.
accessibility: Make only actionable rows interactive. Name a selected Tile and preserve aria-pressed instead of adding click handlers to a generic div.
limitations: ItemGroup supplies list/listitem structure and preserves slotted links; selection, unread counts and operations remain caller-owned.

examples.title: Unread rows, errors and a selectable provider

use: Use Item for one rich object with named content slots. Choose List when collection identity and selection need a shared owner.
guidance.decision: Choose Item for one object with rich title, metadata, media and actions. Use List for a managed collection and DataTable for column comparison.

rules.when: A row has both a main destination and secondary controls.
rules.do: Use a native title link or button for the main action and a separately named target for each secondary action.
rules.avoid: Wrap the complete row in a button containing other buttons or links.
rules.reason: Distinct native targets let people open, select and act on an object without one click triggering a different action.

detect.how: Tab through the item's main action and its secondary controls; each has a distinct name and activating one does not trigger another.

rules.when: An object preview includes title, metadata and independent actions.
rules.do: Use title, description, badge, meta and actions slots; choose actionsPlacement=below when neighboring content needs more width.
rules.avoid: Concatenate a title and count into an anonymous string or slot a whole row into a link that contains another action button.
rules.reason: Explicit slots preserve readable relationships and prevent nested interactive targets.

detect.how: Compare long titles, metadata and actions at narrow width. Each action remains independently reachable and selected or unread treatment follows actual host state.

states.guidance: Place the error with the affected item rather than replacing unrelated list content.
Choose truncation only when the full identifier remains available through an intentional route.

antiSlop.do: Allocate media, metadata and actions according to the object's task.
antiSlop.avoid: Populate every slot with an icon, badge and decorative description by default.
antiSlop.reason: Optional slots should carry information, not force every object into a noisy template.

checks.command: npm run ui:dev; open /design-system#item and verify the documented interaction.

components.title: Label
components.summary: Give a form control a persistent accessible label.
behavior: Label forwards native htmlFor and ref through Radix Label; clicking it targets the associated labelable control.
accessibility: Match htmlFor to the actual input ID or nest the control. Description and error text need their own aria-describedby association.
limitations: Label does not connect help/error text or validate a value; Field shorthand can provide those associations for supported controls.

use: Associate Label with the real control id, keep required or optional wording consistent and use Field when help and errors need coordinated wiring.
avoid: Use a label as an unbound section heading or assume nearby text labels a custom control automatically.
guidance.decision: Choose Label for the persistent visible name of one labelable control. Use Field when the name also needs help or an error.

rules.when: A custom control is nested inside a styled wrapper.
rules.do: Point htmlFor at the actual focusable control id, or use the control's supported labeling relationship.
rules.avoid: Point htmlFor at a non-labelable div or use only placeholder text.
rules.reason: The label must focus and name the control that receives input.

detect.how: Click each label and inspect the control's accessible name. The actual input receives focus, and entering a value does not remove the visible name.

states.guidance: Keep the name readable and explain any required marker consistently.
Keep the label legible even when the associated control is unavailable.

antiSlop.do: Write a short name for the value being entered.
antiSlop.avoid: Use Enter your followed by the same noun in every label.
antiSlop.reason: Repeated instructions lengthen forms without identifying a different field.

antiSlop.do: Write the field purpose in plain words and mark required, optional and unavailable conditions where they matter.
antiSlop.avoid: Use a placeholder as the only name or attach one label to several unrelated controls.
antiSlop.reason: A persistent label lets people identify and return to the intended control.

checks.command: npm run ui:dev; open /design-system#label and verify the documented interaction.

components.title: Menubar
components.summary: Group application menus with keyboard navigation.
behavior: Open menus retain Radix typeahead and directional keys. Shortcut text requires a matching host handler.
Each MenubarMenu owns a trigger and menu content. Action items close normally; checkbox/radio items remain open unless closeOnSelect requests dismissal.
accessibility: Arrow keys move across the menu triggers and within each menu, skipping disabled items. Name icon-only triggers and distinguish an action from a checked selection.
limitations: Menubar models application action menus, not primary website navigation; checked values and operations belong to the host.

omitted.reason: Inset reserves the icon column for a plain row beside rows that carry icons. The example menu has no icons.

use: Group commands by task, keep checked items under their proper radio or checkbox model and keep arrow-key movement between menus working.
avoid: Use Menubar for website destinations or add a shortcut caption without implementing its action binding.
guidance.decision: Choose Menubar for a persistent desktop-style command surface. Use NavigationMenu for website destinations and DropdownMenu for a single object's actions.

rules.when: The top row opens command menus rather than navigating to pages.
rules.do: Group related commands under specific menu names and keep checked preferences controlled.
rules.avoid: Use menuitem behavior for an ordinary collection of destination links.
rules.reason: Command menus have a keyboard model that differs from page navigation.

detect.how: Open categories with keyboard, activate a command and change a checked preference; the row behaves as command menus rather than pretending to be ordinary page navigation.

states.guidance: Reflect the actual view preference in the checkbox or radio item.
Keep unavailable commands meaningful and explain their prerequisite nearby.

antiSlop.do: Keep a small stable set of command categories.
antiSlop.avoid: Build a second application navigation bar from menus labeled after every page.
antiSlop.reason: Competing navigation models make the current location harder to understand.

checks.command: npm run ui:dev; open /design-system#menubar and verify the documented interaction.

components.title: Navigation Menu
components.summary: Navigate between related destinations and expandable groups.
behavior: Radix NavigationMenu coordinates trigger/content pairs and an optional shared viewport; NavigationMenuLink retains native navigation through its child anchor.
accessibility: Keep page destinations as links and disclosure triggers as buttons. Arrow keys move between items and each trigger announces whether its panel is open. Label the navigation landmark.
limitations: Destinations and active-route state are owner-supplied; the menu does not perform routing or authorization.

use: Supply real hrefs and active-route state, group by destination hierarchy and keep the current location understandable without color.
avoid: Use a navigation item for a destructive command or set every clicked item active without observing the router.
guidance.decision: Choose NavigationMenu for top-level destinations with optional descriptive panels. Use Menubar for commands.

rules.when: A destination has supporting links in a disclosure panel.
rules.do: Use real links for destinations and reserve the trigger for opening the panel.
rules.avoid: Use menu actions as destination links or make a heading-only trigger pretend to navigate.
rules.reason: Opening a panel and visiting a page are different actions.

detect.how: Open a panel and follow its destination links with keyboard. Opening does not falsely navigate, and the current marker follows the real destination.

states.guidance: Identify the actual current destination rather than the last hovered panel.
Keep destination links reachable when the panel layout wraps.

antiSlop.do: Group destinations by a clear information hierarchy.
antiSlop.avoid: Put every product feature in an oversized promotional navigation panel.
antiSlop.reason: A navigation panel should shorten route finding rather than become a second landing page.

checks.command: npm run ui:dev; open /design-system#navigation-menu and verify the documented interaction.

components.title: Popover
components.summary: Show a small interactive panel anchored to its trigger.
behavior: Radix open/onOpenChange controls a trigger-anchored region with side/alignment placement. Content portals into V4Scope and honors descendant Escape ownership.
accessibility: Name the popover's purpose through a heading or aria-label. Focus moves in when it opens and back to the trigger when it closes. Choose modal behavior for the task.
limitations: PopoverTitle is a heading, not an automatic dialog label association; connect its ID when the content requires that name.

use: Keep an anchored optional task compact, named and reachable. Use Dialog when the task needs a larger focused workflow.
guidance.decision: Choose Popover for a small contextual picker or form anchored to its trigger. Use Tooltip for a short explanation and Dialog for a longer focused task.

rules.when: An anchored form can be invalid or dirty.
rules.do: Keep the form compact, show field errors in the panel, and let the host decide whether dismissal discards a draft.
rules.avoid: Hide a long multistep task inside a transient panel that closes on outside interaction.
rules.reason: The anchor helps context only while the task remains small and recoverable.

detect.how: Open, validate and dismiss the contextual form with keyboard. Invalid values remain repairable and any unsaved dismissal follows an explicit host policy.

rules.when: A small optional task belongs beside a trigger.
rules.do: Use Popover for local nonmodal content, name interactive content explicitly where needed and keep its actions within available viewport space.
rules.avoid: Use it for a long irreversible workflow or assume PopoverTitle automatically supplies an accessible dialog name.
rules.reason: An anchored panel needs its own readable context and a deliberate name; a heading alone does not wire that relationship.

detect.how: Open at each relevant viewport edge, use its controls and close with Escape. Content stays reachable and focus returns to the trigger without clipping the required actions.

states.guidance: Move focus according to the task and retain the triggering object context.
Keep failed input available for correction rather than closing the panel.

antiSlop.do: Give the panel one specific purpose.
antiSlop.avoid: Use a popover merely to add a second border around an already visible control.
antiSlop.reason: An extra interaction should reveal useful context or reduce real density.

checks.command: npm run ui:dev; open /design-system#popover and verify the documented interaction.

components.title: Progress
components.summary: Expose determinate or indeterminate progress with numeric semantics.
behavior: Progress clamps its ARIA value while preserving explicit over-limit copy. It supports automatic tone, indeterminate activity and a ProgressSteps companion.
accessibility: Name the operation. Indeterminate progress omits a value, and visible over-limit copy explains a value beyond the bound.
limitations: The owner supplies measured progress; indeterminate mode communicates activity without estimating completion or elapsed time.

use: Use determinate progress for measured units and indeterminate activity when the host cannot report completion.
guidance.decision: Choose Progress for measurable completion or an explicitly indeterminate operation. Use Spinner when only pending activity is known and ProgressSteps for named stages.

rules.when: The operation reports a completed count and total.
rules.do: Derive value from those counts and expose a readable unit, such as 32 of 80 records.
rules.avoid: Animate a timer from zero toward 99 percent when the operation reports no completion data.
rules.reason: A percentage claims measurable completion. Unknown duration needs an honest pending state rather than a timer that stalls near completion.

detect.how: Inspect determinate value/max and an unknown-duration state. Numeric completion derives from real completed work, and unknown progress has no invented percentage.

rules.when: A task can report completed units or only pending activity.
rules.do: Supply measured value and max when known, label the quantity and use indeterminate mode when completion is unknown.
rules.avoid: Animate a made-up percentage toward completion, infer an error from a high value alone or announce completion before the host settles.
rules.reason: A progress indicator represents data about real work rather than decoration or a timer.

detect.how: Test zero, completion, out-of-range input and indeterminate work. The displayed quantity follows supplied measurements and success follows actual completion.

states.guidance: Use the indeterminate state and explain what is pending.
Report completion from the actual operation result, not merely a full-looking bar.

antiSlop.do: Show progress near the work it describes.
antiSlop.avoid: Add multiple progress bars for one operation without distinct units.
antiSlop.reason: Duplicate indicators make it unclear which measure determines completion.

components.title: Radio Group
components.summary: Choose one option from a visible group.
behavior: RadioGroup uses one string value with value/defaultValue and onValueChange. Each RadioGroupItem contributes its own value and disabled state.
accessibility: Name the group and each option with explicit labels. Arrow keys move the choice within the group, and each option announces whether it is checked. Associate any group error explicitly.
limitations: RadioGroup does not consume Field context automatically; label the group and connect its description/error explicitly.

use: Use a named RadioGroup for mutually exclusive values. State any requirement and connect validation explicitly.
guidance.decision: Choose RadioGroup when exactly one visible alternative is required. Use Checkbox for independent choices and ToggleGroup for optional pressed tools.

rules.when: The alternatives have different consequences or prices.
rules.do: Label each option and place its explanation beside it; keep one controlled value.
rules.avoid: Assume changing the selected radio persisted the setting before the form saves.
rules.reason: Selection and persistence are separate unless the host applies the choice immediately.

detect.how: Select each permitted alternative and submit or cancel the enclosing form; exactly one value is chosen and selection alone does not falsely claim it was saved.

rules.when: A form presents mutually exclusive choices.
rules.do: Use stable string values and a named group, connect help/error ids explicitly and let the host decide whether an empty value is valid.
rules.avoid: Use ToggleGroup when a required selection must remain, or assume RadioGroup consumes Field context without wiring.
rules.reason: A radio choice and optional pressed tools have different empty-state and labeling contracts.

detect.how: Arrow through enabled choices with a disabled option present. Group name, error description and selected value remain correct before and after validation.

states.guidance: Allow an unset value only if the task permits it and explain the requirement on submit.
Keep the unavailable option's explanation visible when it affects the choice.

antiSlop.do: Write parallel option labels that expose the difference.
antiSlop.avoid: Use a radio list as navigation to unrelated pages.
antiSlop.reason: A radio group communicates one value, not a route menu.

antiSlop.do: Make empty, invalid and policy-disabled selection visible beside ordinary choices.
antiSlop.avoid: Preselect an answer only to make the specimen look complete or use radio buttons for independent flags.
antiSlop.reason: Mutual exclusion and a deliberate empty value must remain understandable.

checks.command: npm run ui:dev; open /design-system#radio-group and verify the documented interaction.

components.title: Resizable
components.summary: Resize adjacent panels using a separator handle.
behavior: Group forwards the installed panel library's orientation and layout callbacks. Panels accept defaultSize/minSize/maxSize; Separator provides drag and keyboard resize behavior.
accessibility: Keep the handle focusable with a visible focus state, announcing its current size and the panel it resizes. Give panel contents useful headings.
limitations: The host owns layout persistence and content adaptation. Installed v4 panel sizes use pixels for numbers and explicit units for percentages, such as '40%'.

omitted.reason: Dropping the grip leaves the same one-pixel divider and drag target.
A disabled handle is the divider without drag or keyboard resizing.

use: Give panel sizes explicit units, choose minimums from usable content and keep the handle keyboard reachable.
avoid: Treat numeric sizes as percentages, persist impossible values or shrink a form until its actions become unreachable.
guidance.decision: Choose Resizable for adjacent work areas that remain usable at their minimum sizes. Use a responsive Grid when the user does not need manual resizing.

rules.when: A split should start at half width and stop at one fifth.
rules.do: Use explicit percentage strings for percentage constraints and choose minimum sizes from the real content; verify both panels at each bound.
rules.avoid: Copy numeric defaultSize 50 and minSize 20 from an older percentage-based API.
rules.reason: The installed API treats numbers as pixels. Even correct percentages can leave a panel too narrow for its title or controls.

detect.how: Move the divider to both minimum bounds using keyboard and pointer, then resize the viewport. Both panels and their labels remain readable at those permitted sizes.

states.guidance: Keep the content usable at each permitted limit.
Retain a discoverable handle and verify keyboard resizing as well as dragging.

antiSlop.do: Add a resize handle only when changing the split helps the work.
antiSlop.avoid: Make every card edge draggable because the library supports it.
antiSlop.reason: Unnecessary handles add interaction without a useful layout choice.

checks.command: npm run ui:dev; open /design-system#resizable and verify the documented interaction.

components.title: Scroll Area
components.summary: Scroll constrained content with a styled scrollbar.
behavior: Radix ScrollArea wraps a native scrolling viewport and a vertical scrollbar; additional ScrollBar parts can request a horizontal orientation.
accessibility: Keep all content and controls in the viewport reachable. A named, focusable scroll region is appropriate when users must scroll it with the keyboard.
limitations: The viewport must be bounded by its layout to scroll; this component neither virtualizes rows nor fetches more content.

omitted.reason: This family has no authored sm/md/lg size option. Its dimensions follow content or its container; examples preserve that API.

use: Bound the viewport through layout, choose the required scroll axis and keep keyboard access to content beyond the initial view.
avoid: Add ScrollArea to an unbounded region expecting it to fetch, virtualize or prevent page overflow automatically.
guidance.decision: Choose ScrollArea for one bounded long region whose surroundings must stay visible. Use ordinary page flow for main reading content.

rules.when: A version list must stay within a fixed-height panel.
rules.do: Set a real height on the region and use the wrapper's built-in vertical scrollbar.
rules.avoid: Insert a second vertical ScrollBar inside ScrollArea or nest several scrolling shells around the same list.
rules.reason: Duplicate and nested scrollbars obscure which region will move.

detect.how: With scrollbars always visible, reach the final row by wheel, keyboard and touch. One intended region scrolls without duplicate bars or whole-page horizontal overflow.

components.title: Sheet
components.summary: Inspect or edit a task in a side panel.

components.title: Skeleton
components.summary: Reserve content space while a resource is loading.

accessibility: Keep decorative loading structure out of the accessibility tree and provide a meaningful loading status where needed.
limitations: Skeleton is visual and aria-hidden; the owner announces loading and replaces the shape with the actual result or error.

examples.title: Pending text and a resource row

antiSlop.avoid: Build elaborate fake dashboards from many pulsing bars.

components.title: Slider
components.summary: Choose a numeric value or range from a bounded scale.
behavior: Radix value/defaultValue is a number array; onValueChange reports live adjustment and onValueCommit reports committed adjustment. Array length determines the number of thumbs.

The filled range and the thumb use the accent in both themes, and the thumb has a 2px on-accent ring. The thumb follows the corner mode: a square in square mode and a rounded square (radius-sm) in soft mode, never a circle. A disabled slider drops to faint and the disabled control surface.
accessibility: Name each thumb with thumbLabels or aria-labelledby; with one shared label, each thumb gets that label plus its position. Each thumb announces its minimum, maximum and value, and arrow keys adjust it.
limitations: The owner chooses units, rounding and when to save. A slider is approximate; provide a numeric input when exact entry matters.

omitted.reason: The same track and thumb on the vertical axis, for a tall side panel. It needs a fixed height.
Reverses the value direction without changing the paint.

avoid: Hide the current number, save on every movement unintentionally or use a slider alone when exact entry is required.
guidance.decision: Choose Slider for an approximate bounded quantity with a visible current value. Use numeric Input when exact typed entry is the main task.

rules.when: A range has two thumbs with different meanings.
rules.do: Name each thumb distinctly, expose its current value, and commit expensive work only at the intended boundary.
rules.avoid: Give both thumbs the same label or persist every intermediate pointer movement without intent.
rules.reason: The user must know which bound is changing and when it takes effect.

detect.how: Adjust each thumb with keyboard and pointer. Distinct names, current numeric values, bounds and units make the changed quantity clear before it is committed.

states.guidance: Update the visible draft while preserving the chosen commit policy.
Show the valid minimum, maximum and unit so endpoints are understandable.

antiSlop.do: Use a slider where continuous adjustment helps compare outcomes.
antiSlop.avoid: Use a long slider to choose a precise account ID or an arbitrary date.
antiSlop.reason: Those values are not approximate quantities and need a different input model.

antiSlop.avoid: Give both ends the same accessible name or claim a committed value from a visual thumb movement alone.

components.title: Sonner

Call toast from @infisical/sonner, not from the sonner package: a plain sonner toast has no toaster id and goes to the app's v3 Toaster instead.

components.title: Spinner
components.summary: Show the Infisical pixel mark while real work remains pending.
behavior: Inline, base and page sizes. Without label the mark stands alone and is decorative. With label it shows that text beside or under the mark inside one polite status.

size="page" centres the mark and label in the available region and may add a short description under the label. delay holds the whole indicator back for that many milliseconds, so a fast request never flashes it, and cancels when unmounted.
The ref reaches the svg mark. className and other props reach the outer element: the svg without a label, the status wrapper with one.

limitations: Spinner communicates activity only. The owner controls when loading starts and ends; description is shown only at page size and only with a label. Do not use animation duration to estimate request completion.

omitted.reason: The default: every specimen here starts at once.
A delayed spinner renders nothing until the delay passes, so a static specimen would be empty. brand-runtime.test.tsx exercises it with fake timers.

use: Mount Spinner only while work is outstanding. Use inline inside a control or line that already supplies context, a labelled base spinner for a pending region, and page size for a whole empty page. Set delay to avoid brief flashes and replace it with the result or recovery on settlement.
avoid: Name both a decorative spinner and its busy parent with repeated announcements, leave a delayed spinner scheduled after unmount, or use a timer to imply the request completed.
guidance.decision: Choose Spinner for any pending activity: bare inside an action, labelled for a region, page size for a page. Use Progress for measurable completion.

rules.when: A saving button already announces its pending label.

rules.avoid: Expose a second live loading message on the icon beside Saving changes.

rules.when: A request for a region takes longer than its initial optimistic delay.
rules.do: Keep the label tied to that request, set delay to avoid a flash, and unmount the spinner when the request succeeds or fails.
rules.avoid: Continue the animation after failure or imply a percentage the request does not report.
rules.reason: Activity indicates outstanding work, not completion or success.

detect.how: The delayed spinner shows nothing before its delay, then its label, and leaves no timer after unmount.

states.guidance: Show the mark only while real work is outstanding. Name the work, such as Loading environments, where the region lacks its own status.
Keep the pending meaning understandable when animation is reduced.

antiSlop.do: Keep indicator size subordinate to the action it accompanies and use one indicator per pending region.
antiSlop.avoid: Turn a compact spinner into a large decorative page centerpiece or mount several synchronized spinners around one operation.

components.title: Switch
components.summary: Apply an immediate boolean setting with its own pending and recovery state.
behavior: Switch applies an immediate boolean setting, with row layout, small size and disabled states. onChange/onCheckedChange belong to the owner. Off is a light grey track with a dimmed knob (white with a hairline in light, grey in dark); on is the accent track (sw-on) with an on-accent ink knob (sw-knob-on). Track and knob follow the corner mode: square in square mode, radius-control and half of it in soft mode. The knob slides 16px (12px at sm) on the fast motion token. Focus draws the 2px ink outline shared with checkbox and radio.
accessibility: Label the switch and keep its name stable when its checked state changes. Do not stage it behind Save.
limitations: Switch reports boolean changes but does not persist or roll them back; the host must represent pending and failed updates truthfully.

omitted.reason: aria-invalid draws the red control border. A switch is rarely a required answer; Field shows the error rendering.
An id and a Label with htmlFor. The Label page shows the association.
Switch exposes controlled checked, disabled and invalid states. Request pending and retry belong to its caller.
Switch exposes controlled checked, disabled and invalid states. Request pending and retry belong to its caller.

avoid: Show the new saved state before the request resolves or combine an immediate Switch with a contradictory Save footer.
guidance.decision: Choose Switch for an immediately applied boolean setting. Use Checkbox when a form stages the change until Save.

rules.when: Turning a setting on starts a request that can fail.
rules.do: Keep the label stable, show pending feedback, and restore or explain the actual saved state on rejection.
rules.avoid: Place an immediate-looking switch behind a separate Save button or leave it on after a rejected change.
rules.reason: The switch communicates a current setting rather than an unsaved draft.

antiSlop.avoid: Change the label between Enable logging and Disable logging with every toggle.
antiSlop.reason: The state already communicates on or off; changing the name makes the control harder to track.

antiSlop.do: Keep the saved value and a named pending result until the local operation succeeds; preserve it on rejection.
antiSlop.avoid: Render the requested value as already saved or leave a pending indicator after failure.
antiSlop.reason: An immediate setting must reflect the actual host result and offer a usable retry.

components.title: Tabs
components.summary: Switch between peer views in the same context.

Both share one measured indicator. A count renders as a neutral Count chip. The panel sits 16px under the track. Overflow scrolls in the selected orientation and reveals the selected tab.

omitted.reason: A side list: the tabs stack and the underline indicator moves to the right edge. Same parts, same keyboard model on the other axis.

The composed TabsList takes the same two values as Tabs and renders the same track.

components.title: Textarea
components.summary: Enter multiline prose with native text editing.

accessibility: Use Field or an explicit label/id, and connect errors with aria-describedby. Keep readOnly values selectable and distinguish disabled inputs from editable ones.
limitations: Textarea edits plain text; syntax highlighting, rich editing and serialization are separate components or host concerns.

use: Use native rows and host validation, retain line breaks and exact draft text and allow enough vertical growth or scrolling to review the entry.

rules.when: The value contains deliberate line breaks or leading spaces.
rules.do: Preserve the literal draft and allow native selection, newline entry and copying.
rules.avoid: Trim, reformat or suppress Enter without an explicit task requirement.
rules.reason: Whitespace can be part of the value and ordinary multiline editing depends on native behavior.

states.guidance: Keep the exact entered text and explain the rejected constraint.

antiSlop.avoid: Use a one-line-high textarea for long policy text or an enormous box for a short note.

components.title: Toggle Group
components.summary: Select one or several pressed options in a compact group.

Host reveal/save promises receive AbortSignal. Identity/revision change invalidates pending work and clears plaintext.

Copy awaits the actual write before success notification. Failures preserve current draft and show recovery. CopyButton size sm/md/lg describes a 32/36/40px host and produces a 24/28/32px nested action, defaulting to sm. iconOnly defaults to false; icon-only actions retain their accessible label.

Escape cancels an unsaved edit and masks the value again. The editor keeps whitespace and normal keyboard editing.

Read-only SecretInput already receives plaintext in memory. Use SensitiveEditor to defer retrieval until explicit reveal.
Plaintext cannot be erased from browser memory reliably; remasking removes rendered/session references only.

components.title: Settings card
components.summary: One setting, or a few that save together, with a footer that shows status and Save.
behavior: The footer shows one status at a time: the hint, Unsaved changes, Saving, Saved for three seconds, the failure message, or the lock reason.
Save runs from the button or Enter in a field. A returned promise shows Saving; a rejection shows the Error's message and keeps the typed values.
Discard appears only while there are changes and calls onDiscard.
locked disables the fields, hides the buttons and shows the reason. tone danger draws the bad line and wash and shows your own actions.
accessibility: The card is a section named by its title, and the footer status is a polite live region.
Fields stay in a native form, so Enter submits.
limitations: The host keeps the values and passes dirty; the card does not compare values itself.
Locked fields use a disabled fieldset, so they look disabled rather than read-only.

use: Use SettingsCard for settings someone changes and saves together, one card per decision.
avoid: Wrap settings that apply instantly, such as a lone Switch, or several unrelated settings in one card.
guidance.decision: Choose SettingsCard when a setting saves explicitly. Use a plain Card and a Toast for settings that apply instantly.

rules.when: A save fails.
rules.do: Reject with an Error whose message says what failed and what to do, and keep what was typed.
rules.avoid: Clear the fields or show a generic Something went wrong.
rules.reason: People should be able to fix the value and save again without retyping.

detect.how: Clear the name in the example and save; the message explains the fix and the field keeps its value.

rules.when: A setting destroys data.
rules.do: Use tone danger, place the card last on the page and open an AlertDialog that names the object from its action.
rules.avoid: Put a destructive action in an ordinary card's Save button.
rules.reason: Destructive settings need a distinct boundary and a confirmation that names what is lost.

detect.how: Check that danger cards come last and that their action confirms with the object's name.

states.guidance: A 6px warn mark and Unsaved changes; Save enables and Discard appears.
The lock icon and the reason replace the buttons.

antiSlop.do: Name the setting with a noun and say what it affects in the description.
antiSlop.avoid: Write instructions such as Use this card to change your name.
antiSlop.reason: The title and fields already say what to do.

components.title: Sidebar
components.summary: The app's navigation beside the inset: tools, sections of rows, footer rows and one account button for the person and their organization.
behavior: The tools row holds the collapse toggle, then search and invite icon buttons with tooltips.
Sections stack rows 1px apart. A labeled section draws its eyebrow with a rule that runs to the sidebar's edge.
A row with children opens one level of pages on a guide line. It opens by itself when it holds the current page, and while closed it shows the sum of its pages' counts.
Collapsing narrows the sidebar to a rail of icons over the slide timing. Labels move into tooltips, counts become dots, section labels become rules and a group opens its pages in a menu to the right.
The account button opens one Switcher: organizations with their plan, organization actions, the person's items, a theme row and the person's own row for their settings.
accessibility: The rows sit in a named nav landmark. Up and Down move between rows and Home and End jump; Tab still reaches every row.
The current page carries aria-current. Rail rows keep their label as the accessible name.
Focus draws the 2px ink outline inside the row, so the scrolling nav never clips it.
The account button is named for the person and the organization, and the popover returns focus to it on close.
limitations: The reference's two-space switch (Home and Organization) is not implemented; pass the sections for the space you show.
The host owns routing: rows call onNavigate or follow href, and the host passes the current id back.
Organizations never show an avatar or icon. The account button shows the person's avatar.

components.title: Snippet
components.summary: Present a selectable one-line command and copy its literal value.
behavior: The prompt is visual context and is never copied. Size defaults to sm32; explicit md is 36px, with nested copy actions at 24/28px.
The read-only input supports selection; copy waits for clipboard fulfillment.
accessibility: Caller supplies an input label; the copy control is separately named.
limitations: Do not imply that copying executes the command or conceals sensitive arguments.

use: Use sm or md for a selectable one-line safe command. The optional prompt is context, and the optional copy action copies value only.
guidance.decision: Choose Snippet for a literal one-line command that can be copied. Use CodeBlock for multiline source and Input for editing.

rules.when: The command is copied into a terminal.
rules.do: Copy the exact provided string only after a real clipboard write and keep the command selectable.
rules.avoid: Add a shell prompt to the copied value or claim copying executed the command.
rules.reason: Clipboard output must be ready to paste without inventing execution state.

detect.how: Copy a command containing quotes and spaces. Clipboard output is the literal command without its decorative prompt, and feedback waits for a fulfilled write.

rules.when: A one-line command appears with a prompt and copy action.
rules.do: Keep value as the exact safe command, use prompt only for visual context and choose the supported sm or md host size without caller padding patches.
rules.avoid: Include the prompt in copied text, imply Copy runs the command or let its nested action make both advertised sizes identical.
rules.reason: Command presentation, clipboard value and action geometry must agree without changing the command's meaning.

detect.how: Compare sm and md with the same long command, then reject and retry copying. Sizes remain distinct, the prompt is excluded and copied bytes equal value exactly.

states.guidance: Report failure and leave the literal command available for manual selection.
Preserve the exact value while allowing horizontal inspection.

antiSlop.do: Give a short label explaining where the command is used.
antiSlop.avoid: Add a Copy button to prose that is not intended to be pasted.
antiSlop.reason: The action should have a clear destination and literal output.

components.title: Table
components.summary: Semantic object tables with a typed data companion for selection and large datasets.
behavior: DataTable composes existing Table parts without imposing ARIA grid keyboard semantics.
DataTable sits in the shared tint frame: the column header row is a 40px uppercase eyebrow row in the frame and the body rows sit on the inset raised surface.
Basic/striped/bordered, controlled sorting, stable selection, empty and load-more.
Sortable headers show the direction with an icon: up for ascending, down for descending and a two-way arrow when the column is not sorted. The sorted header steps up to ink.
Content sizing floors, capped values, pinned action column and optional fixed-height row virtualization.
accessibility: Native table/header/cell semantics, labelled selection and aria-sort buttons.
With virtual rows, screen readers still hear the total row count and each row's real position.
Focus remains on native controls; loading and selected totals announced politely.
limitations: The host sorts data and owns pagination and cross-page selection policy. Header select-all touches eligible loaded rows only.

Virtual tables use one uniform effective row height. rowHeight defaults to a requested 48px minimum; observed enlarged content can raise the shared metric used by rows, slices and spacers. This does not support arbitrary variable-height rows. Supply width/maxWidth for variable columns.
Only a final column may be pinned. Prefer one or two actions per row. Use grow for a flexible resource column; an explicit numeric width takes precedence.
Use text(row) for full hover text when render returns truncated complex content.

use: Use basic, striped or bordered DataTable for row comparison with native table semantics, controlled sort and optional loaded-row selection.
guidance.decision: Choose DataTable for row comparison, sorting and selection. Use DataGrid when cells need spreadsheet editing, range selection or clipboard navigation.

rules.when: A table header selects rows from a paged result.
rules.do: Select eligible loaded rows and keep total or cross-page selection policy explicit in the host.
rules.avoid: Imply select-all includes unloaded records or add ARIA grid roles to a plain table without grid keyboard behavior.
rules.reason: Selection scope and semantics must match what the user can operate.

detect.how: Select-all with ineligible and unloaded rows, then sort/reload by stable id. Only eligible loaded rows change selection and the claimed scope remains accurate.

rules.when: A table exposes both per-row actions and a bulk selection action.
rules.do: Name the selected scope and keep each row action distinct from its selection checkbox. Make loaded-row select-all explicit when other pages exist.
rules.avoid: Use an ambiguous row click for selection and navigation, or claim every result is selected when only loaded ids changed.
rules.reason: The person must know which records an action will affect before committing it.

detect.how: Select a subset, navigate pages and use a row action; row identity, selected count and the operation scope agree, and one target does not activate another.

rules.when: A row-comparison table can virtualize and select loaded records.
rules.do: Use stable ids and meaningful column alignment. Treat rowHeight as a minimum; every row keeps the same height while scrolling, so the list neither jumps nor leaves gaps. Use DataGrid only when spreadsheet editing is required.
rules.avoid: Let a row action make one row taller than the others, treat header selection as all server records or sort the displayed rows without updating the host data.
rules.reason: Scrolling, selection and sorting must all refer to the rows the person sees.

detect.how: Scroll across virtual slices with row actions present, sort and select eligible rows. The measured row height matches the model, scroll position stays stable and selection excludes protected rows.

states.guidance: Show an explanation spanning the table's columns while retaining relevant filters.
Keep every row one height and set explicit column widths when the table is virtualized. Larger content raises all rows above the requested rowHeight.

antiSlop.do: Lead with resource rows. Align comparable values and keep row geometry stationary while hovering or selecting.
antiSlop.avoid: Lift rows on hover, animate loaded totals, replace ordinary metadata with badges or add decorative columns.
antiSlop.reason: Stable lanes support comparison. Counts must describe actual loaded rows and meaningful exceptions belong beside their resource.

components.title: Top bar

behavior: TopBar is 48px tall on a line-soft rule and the inset ground, and sticks to the top of the inset while the page scrolls.

Long crumb labels truncate and keep their full text in the switcher.

AppInset renders the main landmark.
